gap: No result ChatGPT got states that LiTime's RS485 Monitoring Display, its pick #3, works only with three LiTime packs (51.2V 30Ah GC2 Comm, 51.2V 60Ah GC Comm and 51.2V 100Ah GC Comm) and, in LiTime's words, is 'Not compatible with any other brand battery'.
standout_why: I opened the cited cartvoltage.com/best-lithium-battery-meter-golf-cart and the related cartvoltage.com/golf-cart-battery-meter-wrong-lithium. They cover the Junctek KG140F, Renogy 500A, Victron SmartShunt and pack Bluetooth apps, and the Victron 70 V / no-72V limit is already there. Neither page mentions RS485, the LiTime display, or which LiTime models it reads. The first page says Renogy Bluetooth is 'an add-on module', which a named reviewer contradicts. I did not open the cited golf-energy.com PDF. Its title shows it is one battery maker's manual for its own LCD, so it would not cover LiTime model limits.
decides: This narrows ChatGPT's pick #3 to owners of one of three specific LiTime 'Comm' packs. Anyone with another brand, or a LiTime pack outside that list, has to choose a shunt monitor or their pack's own app. For 72V carts, the 10-120V shunt monitors (Junctek KG140F, Renogy 500A) stay the only universal picks. The Renogy should not be bought on the expectation of adding Bluetooth later.
